briefing.headline: The long road to the next Westminster majority
briefing.summary: Begin in January 2025 with the post-2024 Commons, live polling, party resources, and a four-year runway to the next assumed general election.
facts: Seat totals, party holdings, mayoralties, and council control start from the researched scenario data.
The campaign begins on 2025-01-01 and uses 2029-01-01 as the electoral horizon.
assumptions: Polling movement is modelled from authored events, party actions, targeting, and deterministic simulation rules.
The next general election date is a gameplay horizon, not a forecast.
fictionalPremises: Campaign arcs and event choices after scenario start are authored fiction for replayable play.

electoralHorizon.label: Next UK general election
electoralHorizon.description: Build enough support and local strength to turn the next Commons election into a winning result.

primaryObjectives.title: Reach a Commons majority
primaryObjectives.description: Project at least 326 Commons seats before the electoral horizon.

optionalObjectives.title: Create national momentum
optionalObjectives.description: Push your party to 30% in the headline poll.

optionalObjectives.title: Build a campaign war chest
optionalObjectives.description: Hold at least GBP 500,000 in cash before the final year.

optionalObjectives.title: Turn a local moment into proof
optionalObjectives.description: A visible local response has become part of your national argument.

arcs.title: Storm response
arcs.description: A winter storm gives the party a choice between visible local campaigning and a safer national response.

stages.title: First response
stages.summary: The first public response frames whether the party looks present or procedural.

consequence.label: Storm arc: ground response locked in
consequence.summary: The party is now associated with showing up locally when disruption hits.

consequence.label: Storm arc: cautious response locked in
consequence.summary: The party saves resources but leaves little campaign story behind.

arcs.title: Foreign-policy test
arcs.description: An international crisis forces the party to choose between alliance discipline, public caution, and strategic ambiguity.

stages.title: Iran statement
stages.summary: The position taken in the first hours will close off other narratives.

consequence.label: Foreign-policy arc: alliance line locked in
consequence.summary: The party chooses reliability with allies despite domestic risk.

consequence.label: Foreign-policy arc: de-escalation line locked in
consequence.summary: The party foregrounds caution and public war-weariness.

consequence.label: Foreign-policy arc: ambiguity locked in
consequence.summary: The party avoids an immediate split but gains no clear story.
